title: Getting around with empty hands is the CDC line at about 18 months
summary: Most children walk without holding on to anyone or anything by about 18 months, the US CDC says.
body: Nobody to clutch and nothing to lean on: that is the CDC wording, walks without holding on to anyone or anything. The 18-month page places it among things most children do by then. This is independent walking, a real way of getting around, not a two-step burst and not a jog. Arriving at the skill later is not diagnosed here. The month is an American checklist month.

sources.title: Milestones by 18 Months
